hints: Look carefully at the starting DNA at the top, one strand is shaded grey and one is white. After one replication you should still be able to find those two exact original strands.
Remember what semi-conservative means, each new DNA molecule keeps one old strand and gains one brand new strand.
walkthrough:
**Recall how DNA replicates**

DNA replication in eukaryotes is semi-conservative. That is a key word to remember.

It means each original strand acts as a template and is kept, not cut up or pushed to one side.

**Predict what one replication should give**

Start with 1 molecule: 1 grey old strand + 1 white old strand.

After one round, you must get 2 molecules, and each molecule must contain one old strand and one new strand.

**Match to the diagram**

Only option C shows two identical molecules, each with one full grey strand and one full white strand. That perfectly shows one conserved old strand plus one newly made strand in each molecule.

options.A: Shows strands cut in half with old and new pieces mixed in the same strand. This is the dispersive idea, which is incorrect.
options.B: Shows one molecule with two old grey strands and one with two new white strands. This is the conservative idea, which is incorrect.
options.C: Shows two molecules, each with one complete original strand and one complete new strand. This is exactly semi-conservative replication.
options.D: Shows strands with small mixed fragments of old and new DNA. This is another version of the dispersive idea, which is incorrect.
